scope: 75 individually reviewed stranded members; archive convictions were retained without re-judgment.
method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md before edits.
Ran atomscan in slow mode with local traits and dependency following disabled for every member, before and after edits.
Ran cleave facts for every member, including encoded strings and archive metadata.
Read the source control/data paths; decoded embedded Base64, gzip and raw-deflate payloads. Inspected managed IL with dnfile/dncil and native disassembly with rizin.
Inspected ZIP central/local headers and traversal member bodies. Did not extract the decompression bomb.
provenance_and_context: Kali and SecLists packaging supports authorized testing as an alternative explanation. These selected members are functional exploit, credential-recovery, surveillance or remote-command payload implementations, rather than inert documentation or ordinary support libraries. This tips each individual verdict to MALICIOUS in the requested on-machine triage. The verdict does not establish an actual compromise. Operator authorization, invocation, host privileges, runtime compatibility, patch level and listener configuration remain unknown; none is invented here.
encoding_boundary: Base64/compression alone is not treated as evasion. Payload loading and effects were checked in the source and decoded code. PE-magic erasure, where present, is a separate effect.

placement_claims: Remote-thread APIs and API sets belong under process/inject/remote-thread, not DLL injection or an implementation-oriented runtime/call bucket.
WriteProcessMemory/NtWriteVirtualMemory references belong under mem/write/arbitrary; writing memory does not itself transfer execution.
Remote-thread API-only mappings use parent T1055 rather than DLL-injection or thread-hijack subtechniques.

Port-443 listener detection uses parsed literals for source, retains binary text coverage, and explicitly describes a reference. A help comment describing an external Metasploit listener no longer fires.
ancestor_selectors: The fiber-memory-thread-api-profile selector over process/inject no longer accepts bare memory-write observations as injection evidence. Those primitives remain emitted under mem/write; full remote-thread and executable-memory alternatives remain available.
The notable Empire shellcode-module identity can now see relocated writes through its existing mem selector; its required offensive-module declaration still gates the identity.

No live exact directory selectors for process/inject/runtime/call or process/inject/dll required expansion. Exact-ID consumers and live fixture expectations were updated. Historical finding inventories were left unchanged.

members.marker_note: WireTap: records keys, screen, webcam and credential-triggered audio
members.execution_trace: FromBase64String -> GZipStream -> Assembly.Load -> WireT4p.Program.Main. IL dispatches recording commands to keyboard hooks, desktop capture, webcam capture and microphone/system-audio recorders. ListenForPasswords loads credential-related speech grammar and starts recordings when recognized.

members.marker_note: Mimikatz: LSASS/private-key dumping; memory API traits moved
members.execution_trace: Main selects x86/x64 embedded powerkatz bytes, clears MZ bytes, maps sections/imports/relocations, resolves powershell_reflective_mimikatz and invokes it with sekurlsa::logonpasswords or private-key export commands. Native export parses the supplied command line and calls its command dispatcher.

members.marker_note: BypassUAC: injected DLL elevation payload; API traits moved
members.execution_trace: Builds a command batch and elevation DLL, patches target paths for sysprep/cryptbase or cliconfg/NTWDBLIB, starts hidden notepad and writes the reflective DLL into it before remote-thread activation. Removes the temporary payload afterward.

members.marker_note: DCSync: native domain-hash extraction; memory API traits moved
members.execution_trace: Builds lsadump::dcsync /user command strings, reflectively maps native Mimikatz, invokes the command export and parses Hash NTLM output for domain accounts. Remote-thread helpers are present, but do not by themselves establish that the wrapper takes the remote-process branch.

members.marker_note: PowerBreach: polls and evaluates remote callback commands
members.execution_trace: Callback/polling loops invoke the download-and-IEX helper; DNS answers, event logs, ports or packet knocks can gate the callback. The helper relaxes certificate validation and evaluates retrieved code.

members.marker_note: SweetPotato: coerces authentication to launch an impersonated process
members.execution_trace: Base64 -> Assembly.Load -> SweetPotato.Program.main. IL checks required token privileges, triggers PrintSpoofer/DCOM authentication interception, duplicates the resulting token and starts the selected program under it. PrintSpoofer opens a spooler pipe, waits for the client and runs impersonation as that client.

members.marker_note: SharpSecDump: copies remote hives and decrypts SAM and LSA secrets
members.execution_trace: Base64/GZip -> Assembly.Load -> RegQueryValueDemo.Main. Worker callbacks open remote registry/service resources and retrieve hive data. GetBootKey reads the LSA key classes; SAM and LSA parsing decrypt hash/secret records and format reports. The default help option does not remove these capabilities.

members.marker_note: MS16-032: races leaked logon handles for a SYSTEM shell
members.execution_trace: Get-ThreadHandle uses suspended CreateProcessWithLogonW and duplicated handles. Get-SystemToken uses NtImpersonateThread; a competing token-assignment loop races further suspended logon processes to obtain a SYSTEM shell.

members.marker_note: Reflective VNC: injected remote-control server; API traits moved
members.execution_trace: Selects an embedded x86/x64 VNC image, clears its PE magic, maps imports and relocations, invokes the mapped entry point with bind/reverse/password parameters and optionally uses a remote process handle. This is a reflective remote-control payload, not a stock installer.

members.marker_note: Metasploit cradle: hidden remote code execution; help-listener FP fixed
members.execution_trace: Builds a cradle containing certificate-validation bypass and WebClient.DownloadString -> Invoke-Expression, passes it to a new hidden PowerShell process and starts that process. The port-443 listener wording is inside help text describing the external Metasploit listener, not a listener implemented here.

members.marker_note: PowerUp: includes service-command hijacking and password recovery
members.execution_trace: PowerUp includes audits plus callable exploitation helpers: Invoke-ServiceAbuse changes a service image command, starts it and restores the original; Write-HijackDll emits a DLL payload; SiteList/GPP helpers decrypt stored passwords. The concrete exploitation and credential-recovery implementations tip this member toward an attack toolkit payload despite its audit purpose.

members.marker_note: CredStore dumper: enumerates and prints stored password blobs
members.execution_trace: The embedded C# CredEnum invokes CredEnumerateW and converts CredentialBlob pointers to Unicode. The top-level CredManMain call enumerates the resulting records and prints each username/password blob rather than merely documenting the API.

members.marker_note: NetRipper: injected TLS credential interception; API traits moved
members.execution_trace: Inject-NetRipper writes its native DLL into the selected process and starts its reflective loader. Native SSL write hook at 0x10002d80 passes the buffer/length to the log helper with SSL_Write.txt, then calls the original TLS function. The read-hook counterpart records received plaintext; configuration supplies credential search terms.

members.marker_note: CredentialInjection: Winlogon token abuse; memory API traits moved
members.execution_trace: Creates a SYSTEM-accessible named pipe, clones Winlogon, reflectively injects the helper, and transmits domain/username/password/logon-type values to it. The injected helper invokes logon functionality in the privileged process and reports status over the pipe.

members.marker_note: EventVwr bypass: hijacks msc association for silent elevation
members.execution_trace: Writes the supplied launcher to the mscfile shell-open association, launches eventvwr.exe, then removes the override and stored payload properties. This is an auto-elevation association hijack, not ordinary registry administration.

members.marker_note: PrintNightmare: replaces driver DLL to create an administrator
members.execution_trace: Constructs DRIVER_INFO data whose pConfigFile points to the supplied/generated DLL and calls AddPrinterDriverEx with copy flags. The embedded default DLL creates a user and adds it to Administrators; username/password values can be patched before installation.

members.marker_note: PrintDemon: writes a System32 DLL through spooler and adds Run key
members.execution_trace: Creates a printer port aimed at System32/ualapi.dll and uses a RAW printer job to write native payload bytes. A Run-key launcher starts Fax and communicates with the local payload, then removes the DLL and executes the supplied launcher code.

members.marker_note: SpoolSample: coerces printer authentication; memory API traits moved
members.execution_trace: Base64 -> Assembly.Load -> SpoolSample.Main formats target/capture UNC names. Its RDI helper maps the embedded MS-RPRN DLL and calls DoStuff. Native DoStuff -> 0x1800011a4 issues NdrClientCall3 operations 1 and 0x41, passing the capture-server name to the printer-notification call; failure handling explicitly distinguishes successful coerced authentication.

members.marker_note: InveighRelay: captures NTLM authentication and relays service execution
members.execution_trace: The HTTP listener builds NTLM challenges, captures response material into cracking-record queues, and forwards authentication into SMB session setup. Relay execution constructs SCM create/start service requests carrying the selected command.

members.marker_note: Get-System: steals SYSTEM tokens or impersonates a named-pipe client
members.execution_trace: Get-System either creates a local service that connects to a named pipe and impersonates its client, or opens a SYSTEM process token, duplicates it and assigns the impersonation token to the current thread. Existing administrator/token privileges are prerequisites.

members.marker_note: PowerDump: impersonates LSASS and decrypts local SAM password hashes
members.execution_trace: ElevatePrivs obtains and impersonates an LSASS token. DumpHashes reads SAM account records and LSA boot-key material, derives the boot/hash keys, decrypts LM/NT records using the appropriate RC4/AES/DES paths and emits the recovered hashes.

members.marker_note: SharpChromium: decrypts saved logins and exports session cookies
members.execution_trace: DecompressAsm loads SharpChromium. The wrapper enumerates Chrome/Edge profile roots and calls GetCookies/GetSavedLogins, exporting password fields and cookie JSON. IL decrypts the state key through DPAPI and decrypts data blobs through DPAPI or BCrypt GCM before printing credentials.

members.marker_note: SessionGopher: recovers saved remote-session passwords across hosts
members.execution_trace: Enumerates local/remote user SIDs and saved RDP, PuTTY, WinSCP, FileZilla and related session stores through registry/WMI/file APIs. WinSCP password records are decoded with hostname/username-derived context; FileZilla password fields are recovered and results can be exported to CSV. No remote command is inferred from registry-only WMI calls.

members.marker_note: RID hijacker: alters SAM identity records and enables account access
members.execution_trace: Gets SYSTEM through token duplication if necessary, selects a local SAM user record, rewrites its F-field RID bytes and can modify account enablement/password. This changes effective account identity; it is not a read-only SAM inspector.

members.marker_note: SDCLT bypass: hijacks runas command association for elevation
members.execution_trace: Stores the payload and sets the exefile runas IsolatedCommand override, launches sdclt.exe /kickoffelev, then removes override/payload properties. The hijacked association provides the elevated launch.

members.marker_note: PsExec module: executes and deletes a remote command service
members.execution_trace: OpenSCManager targets the selected remote computer, CreateService uses the supplied command, StartService executes it, and DeleteService removes the transient service. Optional admin-share files collect output and are deleted afterward.

members.marker_note: FodHelper bypass: hijacks DelegateExecute then removes overrides
members.execution_trace: Writes an empty DelegateExecute and attacker command under ms-settings shell-open, starts hidden fodhelper.exe, then removes association and payload properties. The registry values and auto-elevating launch jointly establish the bypass.

members.marker_note: Env bypass: hijacks windir for elevated SilentCleanup execution
members.execution_trace: Sets a user windir value containing a hidden PowerShell launcher, invokes the elevated SilentCleanup scheduled task and deletes the windir/payload overrides. This exploits the task's environment expansion rather than merely scheduling ordinary work.

members.marker_note: SharpLoginPrompt: repeats deceptive prompts and prints valid passwords
members.execution_trace: Loads SharpLoginPrompt in memory. IL repeatedly calls CredUIPromptForWindowsCredentials and CredUnPackAuthenticationBuffer, prints username/password/domain, validates credentials and repeats after failure. A separate thread forces the Windows Security prompt to the foreground.

members.marker_note: Jenkins exploit: submits a Groovy process launcher and reads results
members.execution_trace: Creates the Jenkins /script URL, form-encodes a Groovy ProcessBuilder expression containing the supplied command, POSTs it and parses console-result HTML. This exercises an exposed script-console execution surface.

members.marker_note: Keystroke logger: records translated keys with foreground-window titles
members.execution_trace: Repeatedly polls GetAsyncKeyState, translates pressed keys with keyboard state/ToUnicode, attributes them to GetForegroundWindow titles and emits buffered keys with timestamps. This records user input rather than only consuming the application's own UI events.

members.marker_note: JBoss exploit: deploys a remote WAR via JMX and triggers its JSP
members.execution_trace: Constructs a JMX MainDeployer invocation with a remote WAR URL, sends a HEAD request to the management surface, waits, then GETs the deployed JSP path. Optional HTTPS bypasses certificate validation. The actual WAR is an external input.

members.marker_note: Tater: poisons NBNS and reflects NTLM to execute a SYSTEM service
members.execution_trace: Spoofs NBNS responses with guessed transaction IDs, attracts Windows authentication to a local HTTP endpoint and relays NTLM negotiation to local SMB. SCM service creation/start then executes the selected command with greater authority.

members.marker_note: Persistence toolkit: hides profile code and installs WMI reactivation
members.execution_trace: Add-Persistence builds compressed script activation, appends concealed code to PowerShell profiles and creates elevated/user triggers. The WMI path creates __EventFilter, CommandLineEventConsumer and __FilterToConsumerBinding instances; other paths use tasks/Run triggers. Install-SSP also supplies a security-package installation path.

members.marker_note: NTLMExtract: impersonates SYSTEM and decrypts SAM credential records
members.execution_trace: Invoke-AsSystem obtains a privileged process token and runs Get-NTLMLocalPasswordHashes under it. The latter reads SAM V/F data and LSA boot-key fragments and uses AES/DES decryption to reconstruct NTLM records.

members.marker_note: SMBExec: authenticates SMB and runs a transient command service
members.execution_trace: Manually constructs SMB/NTLM/RPC messages, authenticates with supplied password/hash material, opens SCM, creates a command service, starts it and deletes it. The encoded packets implement remote service execution rather than a generic SMB client.

members.marker_note: GPP recovery: sweeps SYSVOL and decrypts stored domain passwords
members.execution_trace: Recursively searches SYSVOL preference XML, selects cpassword fields, decodes Base64 and decrypts with the known GPP AES key, then returns account/password data. Domain accessibility and authorization are not established by the file.

members.marker_note: Password sprayer: tries passwords across accounts while avoiding lockout
members.execution_trace: Enumerates domain users and password policy/lockout counters, removes likely lockout candidates, tries each supplied password across accounts via DirectoryEntry and writes successful user/password pairs. Delays and observation-window waits avoid account lockout.

members.marker_note: ChromeDump: decrypts browser logins and writes plaintext credentials
members.execution_trace: Writes/loads its embedded SQLite provider, opens Chromium Login Data, queries encrypted password fields, calls ProtectedData.Unprotect and emits URL/username/plaintext records; an optional output file also stages logins/history. The SQLite payload itself is a library, but this member is the active credential-export wrapper.

members.marker_note: CredentialPhisher: deceptive prompts capture and validate passwords
members.execution_trace: Builds application-themed notifications and native credential dialogs, unpacks entered secrets, validates them against local/domain authentication, retries as configured and emits a Phished credentials result containing the password. UI wrappers are embedded assemblies rather than proof by name.

members.marker_note: Inveigh: poisons name resolution and records NetNTLM hashes
members.execution_trace: Sends constructed LLMNR/mDNS/NBNS answers redirecting name resolution, challenges HTTP/SMB clients with NTLM, formats captured responses into NetNTLM cracking records and queues/writes those records. Capture and poisoning are concrete paths, not inferred from socket use.

members.marker_note: USB keylogger: decodes USB ETW input and records keys with window titles
members.execution_trace: Base64 -> raw Deflate -> 624640-byte ETW assembly -> startkeyLog. IL creates TraceEventSession instances for USB providers, filters USB2/USB3 transfer payloads, maps USB key codes and enqueues decoded keys. The wrapper drains that queue and groups output by foreground window/time. This uses ETW as an input source, not an ETW-disabling technique.

members.marker_note: Token UAC bypass: filters elevated tokens and spawns an elevated shell
members.execution_trace: Opens an elevated process token, duplicates it, changes integrity information and filters it through NtFilterToken, duplicates the LUA token, impersonates it and invokes CreateProcessWithLogonW for a PowerShell child. The sequence implements the UAC token bypass.

members.marker_note: MS16-135: corrupts bitmap pointers and copies SYSTEM process tokens
members.execution_trace: Stages manager/worker bitmap corruption, establishes Bitmap-Read/Bitmap-Write primitives, walks kernel EPROCESS links, reads the SYSTEM token and overwrites the spawned PowerShell process token. Trigger-Write exercises the vulnerable window/bitmap path.

members.marker_note: TokenManipulation: steals tokens for impersonation and child execution
members.execution_trace: Enumerates and selects process/thread tokens, duplicates them, impersonates a chosen identity and can create a child through CreateProcessAsUserW or CreateProcessWithTokenW. Its SYSTEM path selects privileged token material rather than a caller-supplied credential alone.

members.marker_note: MSBuild runner: stages inline PowerShell tasks and launches through WMI
members.execution_trace: Generates MSBuild CodeTaskFactory XML containing a PowerShell runspace task, stages that file locally or remotely, finds the MSBuild executable and launches the project through local execution or Win32_Process.Create via WMI. The task evaluates the supplied script in the trusted build host.

members.marker_note: FoxDump: uses NSS to decrypt Firefox logins into plaintext output
members.execution_trace: Loads Firefox NSS, resolves PK11SDR_Decrypt, reads the selected profile's logins.json and decrypts username/password entries. It formats the recovered credentials to output or a plaintext file.

members.marker_note: SiteList recovery: sweeps profiles and decrypts stored service passwords
members.execution_trace: Searches profile/program roots for SiteList.xml, decodes each encrypted password, reverses the XOR transformation and decrypts using the fixed TripleDES derivation, then emits DecPassword fields with the site/account data.

members.marker_note: Test Mimikatz: executable credential dumper; memory API traits moved
members.execution_trace: This is executable test-source payload code, not a test assertion or documentation. It selects embedded x86/x64 Mimikatz, reflectively maps it and invokes the native export with LSASS-password/private-key-export commands; the same memory-loading and PE-magic-erasure paths are present as in the server copy.

members.marker_note: PowerShell agent: decrypts remote tasks, executes code and sends files
members.execution_trace: Decrypts session tasking, parses packet types and dispatches them through Process-Tasking. Command cases evaluate supplied code; file cases read/encode local chunks into result packets. A configurable sleep/jitter, kill date and working-hours loop govern task polling. Templates require listener/session configuration before deployment.

members.marker_note: IronPython agent: dispatches remote code and returns local file chunks
members.execution_trace: The packet dispatcher routes received task data into compile/exec and Windows PowerShell runspaces; results are wrapped by packet_handler. File tasking reads, compresses/encodes and sends chunks. C2 transport/session handlers are provided externally; this is agent implementation, not a standalone configured infection.

members.marker_note: Python agent: executes remote code and shells and sends file chunks
members.execution_trace: The packet dispatcher sends remote task data to compile/exec or subprocess shell execution and sends captured output in response packets. File tasking reads local files, compresses/encodes chunks and returns them through packet_handler. Host/session configuration is supplied by the surrounding framework.

members.marker_note: Windows stager: downloads raw code and executes it as a fiber
members.execution_trace: WinMain parses arguments and calls main. main downloads a template-selected host/path with a routing cookie and relaxed HTTPS verification; ExecuteShellcode allocates executable memory, copies the response, sets that buffer as CreateFiber's callback and switches into it. The source still has listener placeholders.

members.marker_note: ASP command shell: runs posted cmd.exe commands and returns output
members.execution_trace: Request.Form(.CMD) becomes cmd.exe /c text passed to WScript.Shell.Run. Output is redirected to a temporary file, read into the HTTP response and deleted. There is no authentication check in this member.

members.marker_note: PHP backdoor: request-driven commands, file reads and uploads
members.execution_trace: Request c flows directly into system(). Other branches accept request-selected paths for file reads/directory listing, move uploaded files to a selected directory and issue supplied SQL queries. Short PHP tags and legacy database APIs require a compatible PHP configuration.

members.marker_note: Perl CGI shell: executes query strings as commands and returns output
members.execution_trace: QUERY_STRING is assigned to req, minimally percent-decoded and interpolated into Perl backticks. Captured output lines are written into the CGI HTML response; arbitrary query text becomes shell syntax.

members.marker_note: Laudanum PHP: authenticated request-driven operating-system shell
members.execution_trace: An IP allowlist and session password check gate the command UI. Authenticated POST command becomes proc_open input, with stdout/stderr appended to the session terminal. Unauthorized IPs receive a decoy 404. Authentication is access control for a deployable shell, not removal of the shell behavior.

members.marker_note: Laudanum ASP: request-driven command execution hidden behind IP gating
members.execution_trace: An IP comparison gates the handler and returns 404 to other clients. Posted cmd text goes to WScript.Shell.Exec and StdOut.ReadAll is rendered to the requester. The allowlist value is an operator-editable condition.

members.marker_note: WordPress template shell: bypasses login and executes posted commands
members.execution_trace: The WordPress template includes ipcheck.php but replaces the session-authentication body guard with if(true), hides the login form with if(false), and retains POST command -> proc_open -> response buffering. Missing include configuration and a compatible legacy PHP runtime affect deployment, not the implemented shell path.

members.marker_note: WordPress plugin shell: request execution and self-immutability commands
members.execution_trace: The cmd request value passes through executeCommand into ReflectionFunction(system), call_user_func alternatives, passthru or system. Top-level commands attempt chmod ugo-w and chattr +i on the file itself. The optional reverse-shell branch uses uninitialized ip/port selector variables, so a working outbound shell is not asserted from this file's default state.

members.marker_note: JSP WAR shell: executes HTTP cmd parameters and returns process output
members.execution_trace: WAR web.xml maps a command JSP. request.getParameter(cmd) flows directly into Runtime.getRuntime().exec; a read loop sends process stdout to the HTTP response. No application authentication is implemented.

members.marker_note: Overlapping ZIP bomb: 190023 entries advertise petabytes of expansion
members.execution_trace: Parsed all 190023 central-directory entries without expansion. Compressed-data intervals overlap: the first entries start only 56 bytes apart while claiming about 34 MB compressed each. Total declared output is 4507981427706459 bytes. Only a bounded prefix was decompressed; no petabyte extraction was attempted.

members.marker_note: Tiny shell source: unrestricted root-ID shell needs existing authority
members.execution_trace: The complete main body calls setresuid(0,0,0), then system(/bin/sh), with no authorization branch or fixed administration command. This is a reusable unrestricted root-shell payload; root authority or an appropriate setuid installation is still required.

members.marker_note: Root shell source: unrestricted UID/GID-zero shell needs authority
members.execution_trace: The complete main body calls setuid(0), setgid(0), then system(/bin/sh), without authorization. A build comment proposes setuid installation; no installed setuid bit or successful privilege gain is inferred from source bytes.

members.marker_note: Root shell2 source: requests root ID then execs unrestricted bash
members.execution_trace: The complete main body calls setuid(0), then execl(/bin/bash, bash, NULL), exposing an unrestricted shell if root authority is available. No exploit that creates that authority is present.
